text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert firing: gateway 5xx rate spike (us-west).
Details: 5m 5xx% = 1.8% (baseline ~0.1%). Triggered pager to @kelly.

kelly: On it. Checking current deploys and upstreams. Can someone grab logs for gateway->edge-fetch?

henry: I see a burst of 502/504s with connection reset to edge-fetch. Trace IDs: 0a3f.., 7b2c.. — looks like upstream timeouts, not gateway NPEs.

alex: Temporarily increased gateway backend timeout from 3s -> 6s for us-west to reduce tail 504s. Command:
```
kubectl set env deploy/gateway TIMEOUT_MS=6000 -n prod-us-west
```
Applied and rolling restart started.

maria: Any customer impact? Are support pages popping?

kelly: Support reports 3 customers (2 dedicated, 1 hosted) saw errors between 02:05-02:12 UTC. No full SLO breach yet but error budget risk if sustained.

henry: Root cause hypothesis: edge-fetch had a partial outage causing increased latency and connection resets. We have retries that amplify 5xx counts. Suggest two parallel mitigations: 1) faster fallback/cached-response path, 2) reduce alert noise by tuning aggregation window + threshold for gateway-level alerts.

alex: Fallback enabled (cache-first) for a subset of routes — reduced visible errors for affected customers.

kelly: Good. For alert tuning: current alert (prod gateway 5xx pct) is firing on 1m window, threshold 0.5%.
Query (PromQL-ish):
```
100 * sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="gateway",code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="gateway"}[1m]))
```
I propose changing to a 5m window and requiring sustained >0.5% for 3/5 evaluation periods, and add an upstream-scoped alert for edge-fetch errors to separate provider issues from our regressions.

henry: Agree. Concrete change: switch to 5m window and require >=0.5% for 3 consecutive evals. Also add label match `{upstream="edge-fetch"}` for provider-specific alert. New query example:
```
100 * sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="gateway",upstream="edge-fetch",code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="gateway",upstream="edge-fetch"}[5m]))
```
This will let us page on provider-level problems only when they are sustained.

maria: Please add a dashboard panel for the upstream latencies and a small table listing affected customers so support can triage quickly.

kelly: Creating dashboard now: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/ops/gateway-upstream-latency (will add heatmap + top-5 trace IDs). Also adding a small JSON note to runbook: "if provider edge-fetch >0.5% 5xx for 15m -> contact provider support + enable fallback".

incident-bot: Created ticket INC-4821 for post-incident tasks. Handoff: paging henry for follow-up and runbook updates.

henry: I'll own alert tuning + dashboard tile. Plan: 1) Update alert rule and eval window, 2) deploy dashboard tile, 3) add onboarding note to runbook, 4) follow up with edge-fetch contact and escalate if we see recurrence within 24h. ETA for alerts+dashboards: ~1.5h.

alex: Logging one more thing — we should avoid shrinking evaluation window too much; we get a lot of noise during CD spikes. The 5m-window + provider-scoped alerts should cut noise without delaying real incidents.

kelly: Sounds good. I'll notify support and keep this channel open for updates. If errors drop to baseline, we'll un-warn and close the on-call handoff.

maria: Thx everyone. Assigning follow-ups in INC-4821 and adding a customer note for the 3 affected customers.

kelly: Temporary mitigations holding, error rate down to 0.15% now. Closing active pager; henry will continue with follow-ups. :thumbsup:
